change: Repair broken internal links and redirect chains
signal: Crawl returns 404/410, or a redirect hop count above one
why: A dead internal link wastes crawl budget and strands the page it pointed at. The fix is mechanical and has no editorial content, so there is nothing for a human to have an opinion about.

change: Regenerate sitemaps and drop non-indexable URLs
signal: Sitemap contains a URL that is noindexed, redirected or missing
why: Search Console reports sitemap URLs that cannot be indexed as errors, which suppresses trust in the whole file.

change: Add width, height, lazy-loading and modern formats to images
signal: Layout shift attributable to an image, or an oversized asset in the build output
why: Missing intrinsic dimensions are one of the most common causes of Cumulative Layout Shift, and the fix cannot alter meaning.

change: Enforce page-weight and script budgets, defer non-critical assets
signal: A build exceeds its declared budget, or field LCP drifts above 2.5s
why: Google's Core Web Vitals thresholds are published and fixed: LCP at or under 2.5s, INP at or under 200ms, CLS at or under 0.1. Budgets keep a site inside them by construction.

change: Fix invalid or incomplete schema.org markup
signal: Validation error, or a required property missing from a type already in use
why: Invalid structured data is silently ignored by search engines, so the markup delivers nothing while appearing present.

change: Introduce a new schema type on a template
signal: Page content matches a type it does not yet declare
why: Declaring a type is a claim about what the page is. A wrong claim is a trust problem, so a human confirms it once per template.

change: Add contextual internal links between related pages
signal: Two pages are topically close but unlinked, or a page sits more than three clicks from home
why: Internal links distribute authority and help engines understand topic clusters. Additions are capped per page so the text stays readable.

change: Rewrite title tags and meta descriptions
signal: High impressions with click-through below the expected rate for that position
why: Titles are brand voice as much as they are search copy. The system drafts and measures; a person decides how the business sounds.

change: Add or rewrite answer-first summary blocks
signal: A query with impressions has no passage on the page that answers it directly
why: Answer engines extract self-contained passages. A block that fully answers one question without surrounding context is the unit they quote.

change: Expand FAQ sets from real queries in Search Console
signal: Recurring question-shaped queries with no matching on-page answer
why: The questions people actually type are better source material than keyword tools, and each one is a citable passage.

signal: Demonstrated query demand the site ranks for but does not serve
why: Publishing pages to chase keywords is what Google's spam policies call scaled content abuse. Every new page needs a human to confirm it earns its place.

change: Test calls to action, layout and form friction
signal: GA4 shows engaged sessions that do not reach the conversion event
why: Ranking better is worthless if the page does not convert. These run as experiments against a holdout so the result is measured, not asserted.

change: Prices, guarantees, legal text and factual claims about the business
signal: Not applicable — permanently out of bounds
why: No autonomous system should be able to change what a business charges or promises. These fields are locked in code and rejected at build time if edited by the loop.

change: robots.txt, noindex, canonical targets and hreflang
signal: Not applicable — permanently out of bounds
why: A single wrong directive can deindex an entire site. The blast radius is too large to automate, so these stay under human control.
